solves.reasoning: (A) embodied — 'a clock is really a process embodied in a machine'; eliminated contradicts this. (B) indefinite — 'repeats itself over and over again for an indefinite period'; definite contradicts the unlimited repetition. (C) regularly — 'quartz crystals vibrate regularly'; irregularly contradicts the regular/steady behavior required for timekeeping.

(A) repetitive — 'the nature of that process is repetitive'; singular contradicts the repeated cycle. (B) iteration — 'here too there is iteration — the repeated burning of molecules of wax'; stagnation (정체) contradicts the repeating burning action. (C) masked — 'although at first masked' — the iterative nature of the candle was not immediately obvious; revealed is the opposite.

(A) yield — 'It seems to yield a smooth time scale but in fact does not'; deny makes no grammatical sense here. (B) decay — 'the decay of atoms of carbon-14 is repetitive'; growth is the opposite of decay. (C) appearance — 'it gives the appearance of being continuous'; absence contradicts 'gives the appearance of'.

② 'limited' is wrong: 'A clock can be almost any process that repeats itself over and over again for an limited period' — the passage says 'indefinite period' (무한한 기간). Limited (제한된) directly contradicts indefinite (무한정한).

④ 'discontinuous' is wrong: 'although on a large scale it gives the appearance of being discontinuous' — the passage says 'continuous'. The point is that radiocarbon decay appears continuous (연속적인) on a large scale even though it is actually repetitive. Discontinuous contradicts this.
② 'ceases' is wrong: 'A clock can be almost any process that ceases itself over and over again' — ceases (멈추다) contradicts 'repeats itself over and over again'. A clock must keep going, not stop.

Blank: 'But here too there is ____' — the context explains the candle too has a repeating process (burning of wax molecules). Iteration = the repetition of a process = matches 'iterative process' used immediately after. Stagnation/variation/progression all contradict the repetitive theme.

Blank: 'a clock is really a process ____ in a machine' — the passage means a clock is a process physically represented/contained within a machine = embodied (구현된). Dissolved/concealed/fragmented all don't fit the meaning of a clock being a physical instantiation of a process.

Blank: 'the ____ of atoms of carbon-14 is repetitive' — radiocarbon dating works by measuring the decay (방사성 붕괴) of carbon-14. Decay is the correct scientific term. Formation/synthesis/accumulation are all opposite processes to decay.
embodied = incorporated (구현된/통합된). Separated (분리된), abandoned (버려진), extracted (추출된) are all antonyms or unrelated. Embodied = given a physical form within = incorporated.

readily = easily (쉽게). 'The only example that comes to mind readily' = can be thought of easily. Reluctantly (마지못해), gradually (점진적으로), rarely (드물게) are all wrong. Readily = without hesitation/difficulty = easily.
yield = produce (산출하다). 'It seems to yield a smooth time scale' = it appears to produce a smooth time scale. Consume (소비), prevent (방지), destroy (파괴) are all wrong. Yield = to give/produce = produce.
indefinite (무한정한/불명확한)의 반의어 = fixed (정해진/확정된). Boundless/unlimited/uncertain are all synonyms of indefinite. Fixed = having a definite limit = direct antonym of indefinite.
masked (가려진/숨겨진)의 반의어 = evident (명확한/분명한). Hidden/concealed/obscured are all synonyms of masked. Evident = clearly visible = direct antonym of masked.

(A) 'Water clocks drip at a steady pace' — here pace = the rate/speed at which something happens (속도, 빠르기). (B) 'She quickened her pace as she walked' — here pace = the speed of walking/steps (걸음/보폭). So (A) = 속도/빠르기 = choice 3.

'involving repetition of a process or set of instructions' = iterative (반복적인/순환적인). The passage specifically uses 'iterative process' to describe the candle burning. Singular (단수의), linear (선형의), random (무작위의) don't match.

Subject = 'A clock can be almost any process that _____(repeat) itself'. The subject of the relative clause = 'process' (3rd person singular). Present tense → 'repeats' (adds -s for 3rd person singular).

'the _____(repeat) burning of molecules of wax' — 'burning' is the noun here; the blank modifies 'burning' as an adjective. 'Repeated burning' = the burning that happens repeatedly. Past participle used as adjective = 'repeated'.

Blank: 'Water clocks drip at a ____ pace' — for clocks to function as timekeepers, they must have a consistent, regular rate. The passage immediately follows with 'quartz crystals vibrate regularly', emphasizing regularity. Steady (일정한/규칙적인) = choice 4. Declining/unpredictable/erratic all suggest inconsistency.

Blank: 'this too is an iterative process, although at first ____' — the candle appears to burn smoothly (not obviously repetitive). Its iterative nature (molecule-by-molecule) is not immediately apparent = masked (가려진). The passage structure mirrors radiocarbon dating which 'appears' continuous but isn't.
